title: Adverb and Adjective Choices in Conversation
titleZh: 会话中副词与形容词的选择
credits: John Russell wrote this story for Learning English. Caty Weaver was the editor.

sentences.en: From VOA Learning English, this is Everyday Grammar.
sentences.zh: 来自美国之音英语学习，这是每日语法。

sentences.en: Imagine two American students are talking outside of their school.
sentences.zh: 想象两名美国学生正在学校外面交谈。

sentences.en: Let’s listen to the imaginary conversation:
sentences.zh: 让我们来听这段虚构的对话：

sentences.en: A: Today is going slow.
sentences.zh: A：今天过得好慢。

sentences.en: B: Yeah.
sentences.zh: B：是啊。

sentences.en: I guess we should study for our grammar test.
sentences.zh: 我想我们该为语法考试复习了。

sentences.en: A: That sounds like a terrible idea.
sentences.zh: A：这听起来真是个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: B: Yeah, but if we don't study, we won't do good on the test.
sentences.zh: B：是啊，可如果我们不复习，考试就考不好。

sentences.en: A: Fine.
sentences.zh: A：好吧。

sentences.en: Let's go study our notes quick.
sentences.zh: 我们去快点看看笔记吧。

sentences.en: Then we can play video games.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就可以玩电子游戏了。

sentences.en: These bad students may hate grammar, but they just taught you some common grammatical structures in conversational American English.
sentences.zh: 这些坏学生也许讨厌语法，可他们刚刚教了你一些日常英语中常见的语法结构。

sentences.en: In today's report, we will study how conversational grammar differs from written and formal grammatical structures.
sentences.zh: 在今天的报道中，我们将讲解日常语法与书面语及正式语法结构的区别。

sentences.en: We will show you how some Americans use adjectives and adverbs in casual conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们会向你展示一些美国人如何在随意交谈中使用形容词和副词。

sentences.en: Adjectives are words that give information about nouns.
sentences.zh: 形容词是用来提供名词信息的词。

sentences.en: They generally appear before nouns, although they also appear after linking verbs.
sentences.zh: 它们通常出现在名词前，不过也出现在系动词之后。

sentences.en: Here are two examples:
sentences.zh: 这里有两个例子：

sentences.en: You are a good student.
sentences.zh: 你是一个好學生。

sentences.en: Learning English is fun.
sentences.zh: 学习英语很有趣。

sentences.en: In the two example sentences, the words "good" and "fun" are adjectives.
sentences.zh: 在这两个例句中，"good"和"fun"这两个词都是形容词。

sentences.en: They are telling you something about a noun.
sentences.zh: 它们在告诉你关于某个名词的信息。

sentences.en: Adverbs are often used to modify adjectives or verbs.
sentences.zh: 副词常被用来修饰形容词或动词。

sentences.en: They give information about reason, manner, time, and so on.
sentences.zh: 它们提供关于原因、方式、时间等信息。

sentences.en: For example, the adverb loudly appears in this sentence:
sentences.zh: 例如，副词loudly出现在这个句子中：

sentences.en: We sang loudly.
sentences.zh: 我们大声地歌唱。

sentences.en: The adverb loudly modifies the past tense verb, sang.
sentences.zh: 副词loudly修饰了过去时态动词sang。

sentences.en: It tells about the way in which the subject, we, sang.
sentences.zh: 它说明了主语we歌唱的方式。

sentences.en: Adverbs often have an –ly ending, but there are many that do not.
sentences.zh: 副词常有-ly结尾，但也有很多没有。

sentences.en: You can read more about adverbs in past Everyday Grammar stories.
sentences.zh: 你可以在以往的"每日语法"故事中阅读更多关于副词的内容。

sentences.en: Let's think back to the conversation we heard at the beginning of the story:
sentences.zh: 让我们回想一下故事开头听到的那段对话：

sentences.en: A: Today is going slow.
sentences.zh: A：今天过得好慢。

sentences.en: B: Yeah.
sentences.zh: B：是啊。

sentences.en: I guess we should study for our grammar test.
sentences.zh: 我猜我们该为语法考试复习了。

sentences.en: A: That sounds like a terrible idea.
sentences.zh: A：这听起来是个糟糕的主意。

sentences.en: B: Yeah, but if we don't study, we won't do good on the test.
sentences.zh: B：是啊，但如果不复习，我们考试就考不好。

sentences.en: A: Fine.
sentences.zh: A：好吧。

sentences.en: Let's go study our notes quick.
sentences.zh: 我们快去快速复习笔记吧。

sentences.en: Then we can play videogames.
sentences.zh: 然后我们就可以玩电子游戏了。

sentences.en: Notice that the words are used differently from what might be taught in an English class.
sentences.zh: 注意，这些词的用法与英语课上所教的不同。

sentences.en: In casual conversation, Americans often use adjective forms in place of adverbs.
sentences.zh: 在随意的对话中，美国人常用形容词形式来代替副词。

sentences.en: They may use adjective forms to modify verbs.
sentences.zh: 他们可能会使用形容词形式来修饰动词。

sentences.en: For example, the students use good – a word that is normally an adjective - as an adverb.
sentences.zh: 例如，学生们使用"good"——一个通常是形容词的词——作为副词。

sentences.en: One student says "we won't do good on the test."
sentences.zh: 一名学生说"我们考试考不好"。

sentences.en: In writing and in formal conversation, Americans generally do not use the word "good" this way.
sentences.zh: 在书面语和正式交谈中，美国人通常不会这样使用"good"这个词。

sentences.en: Instead, they use the word well.
sentences.zh: 相反，他们会使用"well"这个词。

sentences.en: In formal writing or speaking, you would be more likely to see or hear the sentence "we won't do well on the test."
sentences.zh: 在正式写作或口语中，你更有可能看到或听到"我们考试考不好"这样的句子。

sentences.en: Americans also may use an adverb but choose not to say an –ly ending.
sentences.zh: 美国人也可能使用副词，但选择不加-ly后缀。

sentences.en: For example, the student says "today is going slow," instead of "today is going slowly."
sentences.zh: 例如，学生说"今天进展缓慢"，而不是"今天进展缓慢地"。

sentences.en: You would be more likely to read "slowly" in academic writing, write Susan Conrad and Douglas Biber, two English grammar experts.
sentences.zh: 两位英语语法专家苏珊·康拉德和多格拉斯·比伯指出，在学术写作中，你更有可能读到"缓慢地"。

sentences.en: These grammatical structures are not necessarily slang.
sentences.zh: 这些语法结构不一定是俚语。

sentences.en: They are not necessarily impolite, either.
sentences.zh: 它们也不一定是无礼的。

sentences.en: You might hear some of these structures in a restaurant, at a job fair, or even at work.
sentences.zh: 你可能在餐厅、招聘会甚至工作中听到其中一些结构。

sentences.en: For example, a boss might tell an employee "We need to do this quick," about a project that must be completed quickly.
sentences.zh: 例如，老板可能会就一个必须迅速完成的项目对员工说"我们必须快速完成这件事"。

sentences.en: This is the same pattern that the students used in their conversation.
sentences.zh: 这正是学生们在对话中使用的相同模式。

sentences.en: Conrad and Biber say that in formal speech and writing, adjective forms are almost never used to modify verbs.
sentences.zh: 康拉德和比伯说，在正式口语和书面语中，几乎从不使用形容词形式来修饰动词。

sentences.en: In addition, adverbs with –ly endings are more common in writing – particularly in academic and news writing.*
sentences.zh: 此外，带-ly后缀的副词在书面语中更为常见——尤其是在学术和新闻写作中。

sentences.en: The good news is this: we are not asking you to memorize any of the patterns we have talked about today.
sentences.zh: 好消息是：我们并不要求你记住我们今天讨论过的任何模式。

sentences.en: What we hope to do is show you that the grammatical patterns in conversation do not always match the patterns used in formal writing or speech.
sentences.zh: 我们希望做到的是，向你展示对话中的语法结构并不总是与正式写作或口语中使用的模式相符。

sentences.en: There is more flexibility in casual speech.
sentences.zh: 在随意口语中有更大的灵活性。

sentences.en: Understanding this idea will help you understand Americans when they speak, and it will help you sound more natural when you speak to Americans.
sentences.zh: 理解这一概念将帮助你理解美国人的谈话，也会帮助你在与美国人的交流中听起来更自然。

sentences.en: You might also be pleased to know that Americans will not judge you severely if you use an adjective in place of an adverb.
sentences.zh: 你可能还会高兴地了解，如果你用形容词代替副词，美国人不会严厉地评判你。

sentences.en: In fact, they probably would do the same!
sentences.zh: 事实上，他们可能也会这么做！

sentences.en: I'm Jill Robbins.
sentences.zh: 我是吉尔·罗宾斯。

sentences.en: And I'm John Russell.
sentences.zh: 我是约翰·拉塞尔。
